title: Salary Calculator with Salary Sacrifice: Convert Hourly Pay to Annual, Fortnightly, and After-Tax Income
description: Use our salary calculator with salary sacrifice to estimate annual, fortnightly, and after-tax pay from your hourly rate. Includes 2026–27 tax brackets, Medicare levy, and super gu
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top and tax and Medicare deducted.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual pay?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week, so annual gross = hourly × 38 × 52. For part-time or casual work, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The result is your gross annual income before tax, super, and any salary sacrifice arrangements.

faqs.q: What tax and Medicare levy will I pay on my annual salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: 0% up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% from $135,001 to $190,000; 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Our calculator applies these rates to your estimated annual income to give an approximate after-tax figure. Note that the Medicare levy reduction thresholds used are from 2025–26 as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed.

faqs.q: Does the calculator include casual loading or salary sacrifice?
faqs.a: The calculator has a checkbox to add 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading. Salary sacrifice is not deducted; the calculator shows a base estimate before any packaging arrangements. The term 'salary calculator with salary sacrifice' in the title reflects that you can use the result as a starting point before applying salary sacrifice, which reduces taxable income.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you know your hourly rate, you can estimate your annual, fortnightly, and after-tax income using a simple formula. Our salary calculator with salary sacrifice helps you see the numbers before any packaging arrangements. The basic calculation is: **annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For a standard full-time employee, we assume 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Commission for the National Minimum Wage. This gives a straightforward conversion, but remember it assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice.

### The Formula in Practice

Let's say you earn $30 per hour. Working 38 hours a week, your annual gross is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. Your fortnightly pay (before tax) is $30 × 38 × 2 = $2,280. This is the starting point for understanding your total remuneration, including superannuation and tax.

### Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. Award rates may be higher than the minimum, and they vary by industry and role. Our [pay guides](/blog) can help you check applicable rates. When using the calculator, enter your base hourly rate (the rate before casual loading). If you are a casual, tick the checkbox to add 25% loading automatically. Never enter a rate that already includes loading.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. For the $30 per hour example, the super contribution would be $59,280 × 12% = $7,113.60 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means your total employment cost is higher than your gross pay. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains more about how super interacts with salary sacrifice.

### Tax and the Medicare Levy

Once you have your annual gross, you can estimate your tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of the excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: $51,370 plus 45% of the excess over $190,000

In addition, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Our calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. For a single person earning $59,280, the tax would be approximately $4,020 + 30% × ($59,280 - $45,000) = $4,020 + $4,284 = $8,304, plus Medicare levy of $1,185.60, giving total deductions of $9,489.60. After-tax income would be $49,790.40. This is an estimate; your actual tax may differ due to deductions, offsets, or salary sacrifice.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Breakdown

Knowing your fortnightly pay helps with budgeting. For the $30 per hour example, fortnightly gross is $2,280. After tax and Medicare, it would be roughly $1,915. You can use our [the timesheet](/) to track hours and pay. The calculator also shows weekly amounts: simply divide fortnightly by two.

### Average Pay Comparisons

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). All employees total earnings average $1,579.20 per week, which includes part-time workers. These are averages, not medians for any specific job. For job-specific pay, see our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page.

### Salary Sacrifice and the Calculator

While our salary calculator with salary sacrifice does not deduct salary packaging, it provides a base estimate before such arrangements. Salary sacrifice reduces your taxable income, which can lower your tax and Medicare levy. For example, if you salary sacrifice $10,000 into super, your taxable income drops from $59,280 to $49,280, reducing tax. The calculator helps you see the starting point; you can then apply your own packaging figures.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Further Reading

Explore our [reference tables](/data) for more pay benchmarks, or check the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for current rates. For take-home pay after deductions, see [take-home pay](/topics/take-home). If you need to convert a salary to hourly, our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide can help. Casual workers should review [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) to ensure they are paid correctly.
